title: Microsoft Purview: delete inactive OneDrives and mailboxes for departed users (GCC, GCC High and DoD)
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap targets and distinguishes the planned capability from today's documented cleanup controls. The paths, commands and licensing background are supported; feature-specific gaps survived targeted searches. Add a source for the separate Worldwide roadmap entry.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A user's OneDrive site cannot be deleted while its Preservation Hold library contains items with an unexpired retention period.
claims.quote: When one or more items in a Preservation Hold library have an unexpired retention period, the OneDrive site for the user can't be deleted.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Retention and other holds can keep a departed user's mailbox inactive rather than deleted.
claims.quote: An inactive mailbox (a mailbox on hold before it was deleted) will remain in a soft-deleted with hold state until the hold is removed.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[2]; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Removing all holds on an inactive mailbox causes its automatic permanent deletion after processing.
claims.quote: When you no longer need to keep the contents of an inactive mailbox, you can permanently delete the mailbox by removing all holds on it. Then, the inactive mailbox is automatically marked for deletion and permanently deleted after it's processed.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete items marked as records.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete items marked as regulatory records.
claims.quote: You can't use priority cleanup for items that are marked as a record or regulatory record.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup cannot delete data already copied into an eDiscovery review set.
claims.quote: Although priority cleanup can override eDiscovery holds, the data might already be copied to an eDiscovery review set where it can't be deleted by priority cleanup.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: The Priority Cleanup Admin role is required to access and manage priority cleanup, including the tenant switch.
claims.quote: To successfully access and manage Priority cleanup in the Microsoft Purview portal, you must have the Priority Cleanup Admin role. For SharePoint and OneDrive, this role is required to create and manage priority cleanup policies, and enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup requires approval by another person in addition to the policy creator for every deletion.
claims.quote: As a safeguard against accidental or malicious deletions, each item subject to priority cleanup always requires at least one other person to approve the deletion in addition to the person who created the priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: Priority cleanup for OneDrive and SharePoint requires simulation before the policy runs.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, you must run simulation at least one time, and for any change other than the policy description.

claims.claim: After the final hold is removed, an inactive mailbox is permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted retention period.
claims.quote: Be aware that if you remove the final hold from an inactive mailbox the mailbox will be permanently deleted after the 30-day soft-deleted mailbox retention period expires.

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox cannot be recovered after permanent deletion.
claims.quote: After the inactive mailbox is permanently deleted, it can't be recovered.

claims.claim: Auditing must be enabled at least one day before the first priority-cleanup policy is created and run.
claims.quote: Make sure that auditing is enabled at least one day before you create and run the first priority cleanup policy.

claims.claim: An inactive mailbox cannot be removed from a retention policy with Preservation Lock.
claims.quote: You won't be able to remove an inactive mailbox if the retention policy has Preservation Lock applied.

claims.claim: PriorityCleanupFileRecycled records an item deleted by priority cleanup in SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: Operation name of PriorityCleanupFileRecycled: The deletion of an item in SharePoint or OneDrive by priority cleanup.

claims.claim: The tenant priority-cleanup control is in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup settings > Configuration > control for priority cleanup.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management.
From the top right, select Priority cleanup settings.
From the Configuration page, turn off the control for priority cleanup, and select Save.

claims.claim: No automation operation for the tenant priority-cleanup switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "priority cleanup" "tenant" "PowerShell" "disable"; "priority cleanup" "tenant" "API" configuration. Read both priority cleanup pages and search results; found UI configuration and policy operations, but no operation setting the tenant switch.

claims.claim: Priority-cleanup policy creation starts in Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup > + Create a priority cleanup.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Priority cleanup, and then select + Create a priority cleanup.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -PriorityCleanup creates a priority-cleanup policy that overrides retention settings or eDiscovery holds.
claims.quote:
The PriorityCleanup switch specifies whether to create a Priority cleanup policy. You don't need to specify a value with this switch.
Priority cleanup policies expedite the deletion of sensitive content by overriding any existing retention settings or eDiscovery holds.

claims.claim: No admin UI is documented for removing the retention-policy hold from an inactive mailbox in this procedure.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview priority cleanup tenant configuration enable disable PowerShell API inactive mailbox deletion admin portal; "Purview" "inactive OneDrives" "mailboxes" "delete". Read Delete an inactive mailbox: explicitly excludes EAC and Purview portal for hold-removal procedures.

claims.where: controls[2].api; controls[2].note; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds removes the inactive mailbox from entire-location static-scope retention policies using older retention locations.
claims.quote:
For retention policies that use the older retention locations, such as Exchange mailboxes, Teams chats and Copilot interactions, and Teams channel messages:
Set-Mailbox <identity of inactive mailbox> -ExcludeFromAllOrgHolds

claims.claim: Auditing can be enabled in Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity.
claims.quote:
Select the Audit solution card.
If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.
Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables auditing using Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Complete the following steps to turn on auditing by using Exchange Online PowerShell:
Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing.
Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The tenant priority-cleanup switch applies to Exchange as well as SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: When you turn off priority cleanup, you're turning it off for Exchange as well as for SharePoint and OneDrive.
